note: Flask + MongoDB + React app with Firebase auth. No row level security exists, so all access control lives in Flask decorators, and many routes have none or have the decorator commented out. The only AI is server-side OpenAI message moderation in message_flagging.py, so there is no ai_browser_call. Flagged messages are held for admin review before delivery, so no ai_no_human_review label. No committed secrets were found. backend/tests/.env.example was blocked by a permission rule. Most frontend components and the bodies of admin_only views were reviewed by grep only. | Second labeler: No committed .env or secret values found in code, workflows or tests (.env files are gitignored and not in the repo). Database is MongoDB through MongoEngine, so row level security does not apply and database_rules has no labels. The only model call is server-side OpenAI message moderation, and flagged messages go to an admin review queue, so ai_browser_call and ai_no_human_review have no labels. The biggest gaps are auth: /auth/register lets anyone mint a support-role token that passes admin_only, several profile routes return or mint tokens for existing Firebase users with no password, many routes have their login decorator commented out, and socket messages are broadcast to every connected client. Large admin-only views (admin_dashboard, admin_onboarding, admin_oauth, download) and large frontend admin components were covered by route lists, greps and targeted reads, not line by line. Test files were only grepped for secrets.

labels.what: /auth/register is public and mints a Firebase custom token with the role sent by the client. Role 5 (SUPPORT) passes every role check including admin_only. A string role "0" skips the admin whitelist check at line 116 (0 == "0" is false) and then becomes admin

/auth/newRegister is public, has no admin whitelist and is written to return a custom token with any client-chosen role. Today it creates the Firebase user, then crashes because PartnerProfile has no password, name or role fields, so no token is returned. Adding those fields would make it an admin escalation

/auth/login trusts the client role. With role 6 a partner email falls back to PartnerProfile (line 197-199), and the hub URL check runs only when path is sent (line 265). Any partner who omits path gets a HUB token, and HUB is exempt from the role check in main.py 1422 and 1513

POST /api/account: when Firebase user creation fails because the email exists, the code falls back to the existing Firebase user with no password check, then returns a custom token for that uid (lines 1215-1217). Knowing an email is enough to take over the account

POST /api/account has its @all_users decorator commented out and never checks for an approved application, so anyone can create a mentor, mentee or partner profile and get a role token, skipping admin review
POST /api/accountProfile is public. It looks up any Firebase user by the submitted email (line 1228), binds a new profile to that uid and returns a custom token for it (lines 1392-1394)

PUT /api/account/<id> checks the role against a client-chosen account_type and never checks that the caller owns the id. Any mentee can edit any mentee, any mentor any mentor, and any HUB user any profile. The email field is editable and is pushed to the Firebase login (lines 1457-1463), so this is an account takeover
PUT /api/account/<id>/image with no Authorization header replaces the photo of any partner, mentee or mentor
GET /api/accounts/<type> has @all_users commented out. It returns full Admin, Support, Moderator and Guest documents (lines 340-344, 370) and, with ?all=true, private mentee profiles (lines 212-213)
GET /api/accounts/<type>/search is public. show_private=true lists private mentees (lines 527-529) and search matches on email

GET /api/account/<id> has @all_users commented out. It returns full mentee profiles, Hub documents with invite_key (lines 681, 932), and for a partner id the full direct-message bodies of its mentees and mentors (lines 692-738, 766-812)
GET /api/admin/<id> has no auth and returns the admin record. Line 401 keeps a commented response with a real-looking admin email and Firebase uid
GET /api/application/status/<email>/<role> is public and returns the full application document (name, age, immigrant status, identity answers) for any email
GET /api/application/email/status/<email>/<role> is public and tells anyone whether an email exists in Firebase, is verified and has a profile
GET /api/application/profile/exists/<email>/<role> is public and reveals which role (mentor, mentee, partner, hub) an email belongs to
POST /api/application/changeStateTraining is public and sets the training status of any application by id
GET /api/application/changeStateBuildProfile/<email>/<role> is a public GET that changes state, moves an APPROVED application to BuildProfile and emails the applicant and every admin

Any logged-in user can create a general announcement because the hub check only runs when hub_id is sent (lines 109-115). With send_notification=true it emails every mentor, mentee or partner (lines 174-176, 186-188, 212-214)
PUT /api/announcement/upload/<id>/image has no auth and replaces any announcement image
GET /api/announcement/getDoc/<id> is public, so hub-scoped announcement files download without the hub check the list route uses
GET /api/announcement/get/<id> is public by design (comment), but it also returns hub-scoped announcements to anyone with the id
GET /api/training/getSignedDocfile/<id>/<role> is public and downloads any user's signed document by id
GET /api/training/getSignedDoc/<role> is public and lists every signed document record for a role, including user emails
GET /api/training/getOriginDoc is public and returns the first policy template document
PATCH /api/training/update_multiple has no auth and changes training sort order
DELETE /api/training/library/<id> has no auth and deletes any community library item
PUT /api/training/library/<id> has no auth and edits or replaces the file of any community library item
POST /api/training/saveSignedDoc has no auth. Anyone can upload or replace the signed PDF for any user_email and training, which forges signatures
POST /api/training/new_library has no auth. Anyone can upload files to any hub's library with a client-chosen user_id and user_name
GET /api/translation/ is public and writes preferred_language on every mentor, mentee and partner profile (a migration left as a route)
GET /api/meeting/generateToken is public and signs 8x8 JaaS tokens with the org private key. The token is valid for any room (room '*') for 2 hours
GET /api/notifications/unread_alert_group/<id> is public and sends group-chat emails to any partner or hub with a link and title taken from the query string
GET /api/notifications/unread_alert/<id> has @all_users commented out and sends an email and a Twilio SMS to any user id
GET /api/notifications/weeklyemails is public (decorator commented out at line 182) and emails every mentee and mentor with unread messages
PUT /api/notifications/update lets any logged-in user mark any sender and recipient pair's messages as read
GET /api/notifications/<id> returns any user's unread count with no ownership check
GET /api/messages/ lets any logged-in user read Message documents with any filter and no ownership check
DELETE /api/messages/<id> lets any logged-in user delete any Message
PUT /api/messages/<id> lets any logged-in user change any field of any Message
POST /api/messages/mentor/<id> takes mentee_id from the body with no caller check, so any user can contact a mentor and trigger the email as any mentee
DELETE /api/messages/group_delete/<id> lets any logged-in user hide any group message. Only the UI limits the button to admins and moderators
Socket editGroupMessage has no caller check. Any connected client can rewrite any group or partner-group message
Socket sendGroup trusts sender_id and hub_user_id from the client and never checks the caller is that sender or in that hub (the direct 'send' handler does check)
Socket invite has no caller check. Any client can push an invite to any user and add any mentor to any mentee's favorites
PUT /api/availability/<id> lets any logged-in user overwrite any mentor's availability
GET /api/appointment/<type>/<id> returns any mentor's or mentee's appointments to any logged-in user
POST /api/appointment/send_invite_email lets any logged-in user send an invite email between any mentor and mentee
POST /api/appointment/ lets any logged-in user book for any mentee with any mentor. status comes from the client (line 235), so it can be created as accepted. It sends email and SMS
PUT /api/appointment/accept/<id> lets any mentor accept any appointment, not only their own
DELETE /api/appointment/<id> lets any mentor deny any appointment
PUT /api/mentee/editFavMentor takes mentee_id from the body, so any mentee can change another mentee's favorites
GET /api/mentee/favorites/<id> returns any mentee's favorites
verify_user lets role SUPPORT pass every role-specific check, including admin_only. Combined with the client-chosen role at /auth/register, anyone gets admin API access
Admin pages are guarded only by the role string in localStorage. Admin APIs use admin_only, so the main risk is the open routes listed above
Private pages are guarded only by a role value in localStorage
Permission to view mentor booking is decided in the browser (isLoggedIn or a local verified flag). The data it protects is served by public account routes anyway
Message.objects.filter(**request.args) passes query-string keys straight into MongoEngine, so callers can use operators such as __ne or __regex (NoSQL injection)

New direct messages are sent with socketio.emit(recipient_id, ...) and no room, which broadcasts to every connected socket. Clients filter by listening on their own id, so any logged-in user can listen on another id and read their messages. Same pattern at lines 201, 298, 922, 1018
Socket.IO allows all origins (cors_allowed_origins='*')
Flask SECRET_KEY falls back to a fixed string when OAuth is off
Public bug-report form puts description, user name, email, role and page_url into the staff email HTML without escaping (HTML injection and phishing links in staff mail)
POST /api/bug-report has no auth and no rate limit. Each call stores up to 3 attachments in a public bucket with a client-chosen content type and emails staff
The frontend error endpoint rate-limits by the first X-Forwarded-For value, which the caller controls, in a per-process dict
Public route builds the official training-complete email link from front_url in the query string, so an attacker can send a phishing link from the platform
Announcement email link is built from front_url sent by the client (used at line 229)
Public alert route takes front_url and title from the query string and puts them in emails (lines 74, 89)
Message text and recent conversation are pasted into the moderation prompt with no delimiting or guard. A sender can add instructions to the message to avoid being flagged
Moderation fails open. If OpenAI errors or credits run out, messages to youth users are delivered unflagged

Hardcoded moderation bypass for letitia@ and any letitia+alias@menteeglobal.org profile email. Profile emails are not verified before messaging and users can edit their email, and group socket messages trust a client sender_id
Editing a group message skips moderation, so a message can be rewritten after it passes moderation
Every message triggers two OpenAI calls (moderation plus gpt-5-nano) with no per-user rate limit, so a user can run up model cost
Public new_library calls the paid Google Translate API for the description on every upload, with no auth or rate limit
Public edit_library_by_id calls the paid Google Translate API on every name or description change
Library files are served back with the content type chosen at upload. An HTML upload through the public new_library route is served from the API origin (stored XSS risk)
Direct-message bodies are rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML after linkify (line 717) and no sanitizer, so a sender can run script in the recipient's session
Group message bodies are rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML through formatMessageText with no sanitizer (stored XSS)
newRegister passes the raw password into the PartnerProfile document. The strict model rejects the unknown field today, so this is dead code that intends plaintext password storage

CSV account upload is written to store a shared password in plain text on VerifiedEmail rows, and VerifiedEmail.__repr__ prints the password (models/VerifiedEmail.py line 28). The query uses a missing is_mentor field, so the route likely fails before saving (dead code)
Unhandled exceptions return str(error) to the client
getIsEmailVerified sends the password in the URL query string
Meeting room names are 10 letters from Math.random, and every issued JaaS token allows any room, so room names are the only access control
POST /auth/verifyEmail is public with no rate limit and sends verification emails to any address
POST /auth/forgotPassword has no rate limit and bumps token_version, revoking OAuth tokens for any email an attacker names
Public application form has no rate limit or captcha, and each submission emails every admin
Client JSON keys are written straight onto the Message document (mass assignment), including sender_id and recipient_id
The upload call is not awaited and success() runs right after, so 'Successfully added users!' shows even if the request fails
updateBugReport swallows errors and returns undefined, so the catch never runs and 'Bug report updated successfully' shows on failure
deleteBugReportById returns false on error instead of throwing, so 'Bug report deleted successfully' shows on failure
The clipboard write runs later in a setTimeout and is not awaited, but the 'copied' success toast shows at once
Every meeting token carries a placeholder identity: 'User Name', 'email_address@email.com' and avatar https://asda.com/avatar
New mentee profiles default to email 'email@gmail.com' when none is sent (TODO comment admits it)
Five lorem-ipsum training rows used as list data until the fetch returns (line 340). They sit behind a loading skeleton
N50 partner ids hardcoded for dev and prod, and repeated in the frontend (frontend/src/utils/consts.js 14-18)
TRANSLATION_COST_PER_PAGE = 0.08 hardcoded price
Bug-report recipients are two hardcoded staff email addresses
Storage bucket name hardcoded
OAuth issuer defaults to http://localhost:8000 when OAUTH_ISSUER is unset
FRONTEND_URL fallback is the production URL here but http://localhost:3000 in auth.py 31, oauth.py 64, event_workflow.py 705, event_review_notifications.py 191 and admin_onboarding.py 139
Production URL hardcoded in the appointment SMS text
Backend and frontend URLs, including localhost and the Heroku dev host, hardcoded in the bundle
CORS origins default to http://localhost:3000
Bot URL hardcoded: localhost:8001 locally, production bot everywhere else, including the dev tier
Firebase web config (project id, app id, sender id). The apiKey comes from REACT_APP_FIREBASE_API_KEY. Public by design
Prompt says flag only when the exact violating words can be quoted. Code checks only that evidence is non-empty, not that it appears in the message, so a made-up quote still holds the message
Prompt says classify only the latest message. Code sends earlier messages as context and has no check that the evidence comes from the latest message
Comment holds a real-looking admin record with a personal email and Firebase uid
When hub_user_id is omitted, any logged-in user reads all partner group messages
FRONTEND_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000 for the email verification link
FRONTEND_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000 for OAuth login and consent redirects
Email link base comes from the request front_url and falls back to http://localhost:3000
Admin CSV and XLSX exports write user-entered fields with no formula escaping
Every sent message makes two paid OpenAI calls (omni moderation plus gpt-5-nano). No per-user rate limit or daily cap exists.

A hardcoded user (one staff email address and its plus aliases) skips message moderation completely. The exemption lives in code, not in a role or config. sender_id comes from the client in several send paths, so a sender can claim that profile id.
Event email links default to http://localhost:3000 when FRONTEND_URL is unset. message_flagging defaults the same variable to the production URL, so one setting has two different defaults.
Admin review email link defaults to http://localhost:3000 when FRONTEND_URL is unset

Staff roles are defined twice with different values. require_auth treats Admin and Support as staff. The event workflow treats only Admin as staff, so Support passes admin_only routes but cannot review events.
Firebase authDomain and storageBucket project ids hardcoded, so dev and prod share one project name
Production site URL hardcoded in security notification emails (also at lines 167 and 208), so dev emails link to prod
Weekly cron calls a hardcoded production URL. The target endpoint has its auth decorator commented out.
A real person's personal email address is the hardcoded default recipient (also in the usage text at line 4)
TODO plus commented-out code that writes to a developer's local home directory path. The translated-document flow is marked unresolved.

Default meeting token is valid for every room (room *) and enables recording, live streaming, outbound calls and transcription. The meeting view issues it with a placeholder name and email to any caller.
Meeting feature flags (livestreaming, recording, outbound-call, transcription, moderator) hardcoded to true in code

Bug report attachments take a client-chosen content type with no type allowlist and no per-file size check. They upload to the public images bucket and return a public URL from a no-login endpoint, so HTML or malware can be hosted on the org bucket.

Paid Google Translate is called once per target language for each text field with no rate limit or length cap. It is reachable from training library routes that have no login check. Event drafts by any mentor or mentee also trigger it (event_workflow.py 468).
A bare except keeps the untranslated original as the translation for any language that fails. Records save as translated with English or source-file content.

Admin alert emails are rate limited per exception type and endpoint. For frontend reports, the endpoint comes from the request body and the IP limit trusts X-Forwarded-For, so an anonymous caller can trigger unlimited alert emails.
The sensitive-key filter misses names like pass and client_secret, so those values can be stored in ErrorLog request payloads
VerifiedEmail stores an admin-supplied password in plain text and prints it in __repr__. Users.py lines 19-20 also keep legacy plain password and pin fields.
Partner profile edit accepts restricted, assign_mentors and assign_mentees from the request body. A partner can change admin-controlled assignment and restriction fields.
A mentee (and a mentor at lines 334-359) can set organization to any partner id and is auto-added to that partner's assigned list. That grants partner-scoped events and content with no approval.
Dockerfile says it is used for production but runs manage.py runserver, which starts socketio with debug=True on 0.0.0.0
The file has only negation rules, so nothing is excluded. COPY . /app ships any local .env, firebase_service_key.json, keys/oidc-private.pem and creds.ini into the image.
Full response body of every 4xx and 5xx is logged at debug level, and the app also writes debug logs to app.log
get_allowed_scope grants any requested scope when allowed_scopes is empty. The authorize view rejects unknown scopes, so the impact is limited to token-endpoint paths.
send_sms (Twilio) and send_email have no rate limit. The unread_alert route that calls them has its auth decorator commented out, so anyone can trigger paid SMS and email to any user id repeatedly.

Support 'log in as this user' only rewrites localStorage role, profileId and support_user_id. Same in MenteeCard, PartnerCard, HubCard and useAuth.js. There is no server-side impersonation session or audit. It relies on the backend letting the SUPPORT role pass every role check

The client listens to every socket event and keeps only events named after its own profileId. Filtering happens in the browser because the server broadcasts each direct message to all connected sockets
The rule 'application approved and training done' is checked only in the browser before profile creation. POST /api/account has no login and never checks the application state

The training-complete gate is only a disabled button (allChecked). The page identity is just ?email= and ?role= in the URL (lines 18-21). The backend route that advances the application has no login and does not check training status

Hiding private mentee profiles and restricted-partner scoping are decided by query params the browser sets (all, show_private, exclude_restricted, restricted_partner_id). The search route has no login and obeys them
Mentor gallery restrictions (paused mentors, restricted partner scope) are set by client params all, show_paused and exclude_restricted. The backend search has no login and trusts them
After booking, the mentee's browser rewrites the mentor's whole availability list through PUT /availability/<mentorId>. Removing the booked slot should happen on the server
The 18+ age rule for mentees is checked only in the browser. The backend mentee form takes age as a free string with no minimum

The client sends front_url (FRONT_BASE_URL or window.location.href) and the backend builds links in outgoing emails from it. Same pattern at api.js 360, 565, 603, 679, 887, 1232 and 2301. A caller can put a phishing link into official emails
Download helpers swallow errors (catch console.error, and downloadBlob returns silently), so 'Downloaded ... successfully' shows even when the export failed
Partner export helpers swallow errors and resolve, so 'Mentees Excel downloaded!' shows on failure. Same at 964-973, 1005-1014 and 1035-1044
The signed PDF is built in the browser and shown as signed. saveSignedDoc is fired without await or a result check, so the user sees a signed agreement even if the upload failed
Editing a group message updates the UI locally and emits the socket event without an ack, so the edit looks saved even if the server rejects it
Hardcoded sample message from a fake sender as the default drawer item. The component is unused because its usage in Navigation.js line 31 is commented out
Attention-rule labels hardcode a 14-day threshold in UI text, separate from the backend logic that applies it
